s: Adonis is a youth
q: He, born of his own sister and of his grandfather, who, so lately enclosed in a tree, was so lately born, and but just now a most beauteous infant, is now a youth, now a man, {and} now more beauteous than he {was before}.

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Venus gives the golden apples (to Hippomenes as aid in the race)
q: Hence, by chance as I was coming, I carried three golden apples, that I had plucked, in my hand; and being visible to none but him, I approached Hippomenes, and I showed him what {was to be} the use of them.

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Atalanta is daughter of Schœneus
q: the daughter of Schœneus regards him with a benign countenance

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Atalanta is faster than the suitors (in running)
q: I am not,’ says she, ‘to be gained, unless first surpassed in speed. Engage with me in running

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Atalanta is beautiful beauty (exceptionally)
q: Nor couldst thou have said, whether she was more distinguished in the merit of her swiftness, or in the excellence of her beauty.

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Atalanta is single single life (after receiving the oracle's prophecy)
q: Alarmed with the response of the God, she lives a single life in the shady woods

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Atalanta and Hippomenes' marriage is a marriage
q: Both a wife and a wedding shall be given as the reward of the swift;

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Atalanta and Hippomenes' marriage is stained with blood (as a hazardous alliance)
q: Stranger, while {still} thou mayst, begone, and abandon an alliance stained with blood.

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Adonis is educated by the Naiads
q: Adonis is educated by the Naiads.

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Hippomenes is a descendant of Neptune (fourth in descent)
q: And is it not, besides, because he is reckoned fourth in descent from the {monarch} of the sea?

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Hippomenes is son of Megareus
q: For my father was Megareus, Onchestius his;[57] Neptune was his grandsire;

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Hippomenes wins the race (by using the golden apples)
q: the virgin was outrun, and the conqueror obtained the prize.

l: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books VIII-XV
s: Hippomenes is transformed into a lion (with Atalanta as punishment for defiling the sanctuary)
q: Wherefore yellow manes cover their necks so lately smooth; their fingers are bent into claws, of their shoulders are made fore-legs;[62] their whole weight passes into their breasts.
